chunks: Even though you bring all the proof to the people of the Book they will not face the direction you turn to, nor you theirs, nor will they follow each other's direction. And if you follow their whims after all the knowledge that has reached you, then surely you will be among transgressors.
ai.seo_question: Why did the People of the Book not follow the Prophet's qiblah despite his clear proofs?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores the distinct theological identity of the Ahl al-Kitab, highlighting their divergence not merely in ritual but in core belief, thereby justifying the Prophet's steadfast adherence to divine command over popular consensus. The warning against following 'ahwa' (whims/desires) serves as a broader principle for the Imams and the faithful to maintain doctrinal purity amidst pluralistic influences. This establishes the qiblah as a symbol of unified submission to God's will, distinct from the fragmented traditions of previous scriptures.
